[SWS_CM_00824] Minimum Send Interval monitoring for GetHandlers calls by the client
⌈
To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each Get() of the respective
field class shall have a configurable Minimum Send Interval (cf. ServiceInterfaceDe-
ploymentElement.minimumSendInterval), which specifies the minimum amount of time
that shall pass between two consecutive calls of GetHandlers by the client, i.e., the
Minimum Send Interval limits the maximum Tx frequency of a given Get() call for a
Field in the network. If the application tries to Field::Get() a field value, by in-
voking Get() of the respective field class, ara::com shall check, whether the time
since the last successful handover of the Get() call the underlying transmission layer
is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval
is not violated. If the Get() handler has never been invoked before, this shall also
successfully pass the Minimum Send Interval check. If the Minimum Send Interval is
not violated, ara::com shall process the Field::Get() call by handing it over to the
transmission layer. The time of handover shall count as start of the new Minimum Send
Interval monitoring. If the Minimum Send Interval is violated, ara::com shall discard
the Field::Get() call, and return the error code ComErrc::kMinimumSendIn-
tervalViolationError (see [SWS_CM_10432]) shall be returned via the ara::
core::Future of the Get() of the respective field class. The Minimum Send Inter-
val shall only be check on the client side, i.e., by the instance that actually invokes the
Field::Get() call and not by the server/provider, which returns the corresponding
Field value by answering the Field::Get() call. If the configured Minimum Send In-
terval (ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement.minimumSendInterval) of a Field::Get
() of the respective field class has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring
shall not be active for the corresponding Field::Get().
⌋
